title: Public-shadow nonidentifiability
claim: No criterion whose input is restricted to a public/report shadow can determine cross-carrier predictive transport or lineage over a class containing public-equivalent but predictively distinct systems.
witness: Two finite machines share every admitted public trace but diverge on a hidden continuation probe after handoff.
proof_spine: Construct observationally equivalent source/target pairs; swap the hidden transition; invoke input invariance of the criterion.
assumptions: finite admitted interface; hidden alternatives allowed
falsifier: A proof that the declared public interface is continuation-complete for the model class.
nonclaim: Does not prove hidden structure is consciousness-relevant.

title: Symmetric-duplication unique-selection impossibility
claim: A source-relative rule invariant under target automorphisms cannot select exactly one of two perfectly symmetric qualifying targets.
witness: One source and two isomorphic targets exchanged by an automorphism that fixes all admissible evidence.
proof_spine: Assume unique selection; apply the automorphism; invariance forces the selected target to map to itself, contradicting target exchange.
falsifier: An admissible asymmetry not fixed by the automorphism.
nonclaim: Does not decide whether both, neither, or a relation-valued pair should count as successors.

title: Predictive-quotient insufficiency for the full package
claim: Equality or bisimilarity of a selected predictive quotient does not imply preservation of independent binding, temporal-closure, action-credit, or viability predicates.
witness: Two systems share quotient transitions but differ on a hidden joint-binding bit or repair dependency.
proof_spine: Take a product extension invisible to quotient tests but visible to a package predicate.
assumptions: package predicates not definable from the quotient
falsifier: A definability theorem deriving every retained package clause from the quotient.
nonclaim: Does not show predictive structure is unimportant.

title: Branchwise preservation does not imply recombination preservation
claim: Separate preservation of every branch marginal does not imply preservation of joint recombination information.
witness: Matched branch states with different parity/correlation revealed only after recombination.
proof_spine: Use two joint distributions or automata with identical marginals and distinct joint probe values.
falsifier: A factorization theorem showing all joint probes are determined by branch marginals.
nonclaim: Does not require quantum structure; a finite classical witness suffices.

title: Permanent decoder support is not target autonomy
claim: A target whose relevant package exists only while an external decoder/controller remains active fails a target-native autonomy predicate defined by withdrawal.
witness: Encoded state with correct decoded behavior during support and immediate collapse when decoder is removed.
proof_spine: Evaluate the autonomy predicate under its declared intervention; the target-only trajectory exits the maintained set.
assumptions: autonomy defined by target-side maintenance after withdrawal
falsifier: The decoder is included in the independently declared target carrier or is endogenously regenerated by it.
nonclaim: Does not say externally supported systems are unconscious.

title: Route independence requires trivial holonomy or equivalent confluence
claim: Endpoint data alone cannot guarantee route-independent transport when admissible loops act nontrivially on retained state or history.
witness: A two-route finite bridge whose closed loop flips a memory or predictive label.
proof_spine: Compose one route with the inverse of the other; nontrivial loop action yields distinct transported results.
assumptions: retained object carries the loop action
falsifier: A flatness/confluence proof on the full retained object.
nonclaim: Does not require every valid criterion to be route-independent.

title: Small global residual can hide a catastrophic local defect
claim: No scalar average error bound alone protects a hard local predicate over model classes permitting error concentration.
witness: Move an epsilon-sized fraction of total state error onto the sole viability-critical transition.
proof_spine: Construct a sequence with aggregate residual tending to zero while the hard predicate remains false.
assumptions: localized hard gates; aggregate metric permits concentration
falsifier: A stability/Lipschitz theorem tying the global metric to every critical local margin.
nonclaim: Does not rule out typed vector metrics or certified margins.

title: Local certificates do not imply global gluing
claim: Patchwise valid bridge or clause witnesses need not define one globally compatible target object.
witness: A finite cover with pairwise local witnesses and a nontrivial cocycle/critical triple obstruction.
proof_spine: Exhibit incompatible overlap equations despite local satisfaction.
assumptions: global compatibility is an independent predicate
falsifier: A sheaf/closure theorem proving local-to-global extension for the chosen package.
nonclaim: Does not say local tests are useless.

title: Endpoint equality does not establish process lineage
claim: A criterion depending only on source and target endpoint structures cannot distinguish a live handoff from an independently constructed duplicate with the same endpoints.
witness: Two episodes share identical endpoint states; only one contains causal overlap or a source-generated process path.
proof_spine: Endpoint inputs are equal, so endpoint-only criteria return equal verdicts despite different histories.
falsifier: A theorem that lineage is fully supervenient on the declared endpoints.
nonclaim: Does not establish that causal overlap is sufficient.

title: Temporal-gap underdetermination without dormancy semantics
claim: A gap containing no maintained target package is neither continuation nor failure by structural data alone unless a dormancy/recovery rule is added.
witness: Two reconstructions after identical empty intervals, one source-derived and one independently generated, with equal endpoint state.
proof_spine: Remove history/dormancy data; the endpoint evidence is identical while intended ancestry differs.
assumptions: no canonical now or persistence through emptiness
falsifier: A noncircular dormancy token and recovery law that uniquely carries the relevant object.
nonclaim: Does not prove gaps are fatal under every ontology.

title: Carrier-individuation trivialization
claim: If carrier identity is defined by whatever preserves the desired object, cross-carrier transport becomes circular or collapses to same-carrier re-encoding.
witness: Choose carrier equivalence after observing the desired verdict so every successful episode is redescribed as one carrier.
proof_spine: Show the transport predicate is invariant by definition rather than theorem, eliminating falsifying cases.
assumptions: carrier tokens must be individuated independently
falsifier: An exogenous carrier rule fixed before candidate evaluation.
nonclaim: Does not privilege biological or spatial carrier boundaries.

title: Bridge-composition noncongruence under route memory
claim: Pairwise admissible bridges need not compose to the same verdict as a direct bridge when the retained object contains route memory or intermediate-support effects.
witness: S→M and M→T each preserve local data, while S→T loop comparison flips a retained marker.
proof_spine: Compute direct and composite actions; their difference is the holonomy/critical-pair residue.
falsifier: A functoriality or confluence theorem on all retained data.
nonclaim: Does not require composition to be total.

title: Finite-instrument nonidentifiability over an open continuation class
claim: A finite set of probes cannot identify a unique continuation structure over an unrestricted class closed under hidden extensions.
witness: Extend any probed finite machine with an unprobed state reached after the last admitted horizon.
proof_spine: Diagonalize beyond the finite probe set while preserving every observed answer.
assumptions: open class; finite instrument; hidden extensions
falsifier: A finite model class with a proved complete distinguishing set.
nonclaim: Does not preclude exact finite toy theorems.

title: Certificate match is independent of certificate soundness
claim: Matching a structural certificate across carriers does not entail that the certificate tracks consciousness unless certificate soundness is separately assumed or established.
witness: Two interpretations of the same formal certificate, one psychophysically sound and one not, share all structural facts.
proof_spine: The structural premises are invariant while the ontological interpretation varies.
assumptions: certificate soundness not derivable from structural syntax alone
falsifier: A valid soundness theorem connecting the certificate to the intended ontological predicate.
nonclaim: Does not refute the certificate's structural usefulness.

title: Structural lineage does not entail numerical personal identity
claim: Any structural lineage relation that permits nontrivial fission or fusion cannot be identical to strict numerical identity, which is one-one and transitive in the ordinary sense.
witness: One source relates to two symmetric successors, or two sources relate to one fusion target.
proof_spine: Compare the arity of the relation with identity's uniqueness laws.
falsifier: A revised identity concept explicitly relation-valued and no longer numerical identity.
nonclaim: Does not decide what matters for survival.

title: Symmetry–uniqueness–branch-success trilemma
claim: In exact symmetric duplication, no criterion can simultaneously be symmetry-invariant, award success to each qualifying branch, and return exactly one unique continuer.
witness: One source, two symmetric exact targets, both satisfying all branch-local gates.
proof_spine: Symmetry gives equal verdicts; branch success makes both positive; uniqueness forbids both.
falsifier: Reject one horn: add asymmetry, deny one branch, or make continuation relation-valued.
nonclaim: Does not privilege a particular horn.

title: Fusion conflict for exclusive action-credit ledgers
claim: Two source histories assigning exclusive credit or incompatible self-coordinates cannot be naively fused into one coherent ledger without a conflict-resolution rule that changes at least one input claim.
witness: Sources credit incompatible agents for the same exclusive event; target copies both ledgers.
proof_spine: The conjunction violates exclusivity; any coherent target must revise, contextualize, or branch the claims.
falsifier: A typed provenance algebra that embeds both claims without contradiction.
nonclaim: Does not rule out fusion with transformed provenance.

title: Essential external support precludes target-native autonomy
claim: If removal of an external support process necessarily destroys every realization of the declared package, the package is not autonomous on the declared target carrier.
witness: A target whose temporal order, decoding, repair, or resource regulation is permanently supplied from outside the carrier boundary.
proof_spine: Apply the declared withdrawal intervention and show no target-only invariant region remains.
assumptions: declared target boundary; target-native autonomy definition
falsifier: Redraw the carrier boundary before evaluation or prove endogenous regeneration after finite bootstrapping.
nonclaim: Does not settle consciousness of extended or distributed systems; it tests the declared boundary.
